instruction: Examine the spreadsheet on the desktop, which contains a record of books read in 2022. Take the website https://howlongtoread.com/ as a reference to identify the Fantasy genre book with the slowest reading pace, measured in words per day. I have an empty document named 'book_list_result.docx' on the desktop; please open it and record the title there.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires filtering by Fantasy genre then finding the slowest. Verified with Python: Fantasy books are 'Fire and Blood' (4797.59 words/day) and 'American Gods' (3797.3 words/day). 'American Gods' is the slowest Fantasy book. Evaluator checks if DOCX contains this title.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Binary: 1.0 if 'American Gods' found in DOCX, 0.0 otherwise

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly extracts text from DOCX file using env.controller.get_file() and python-docx library, extracting all paragraph text which is appropriate for finding a book title
Metric logic correctly performs case-insensitive substring matching to check if 'American Gods' is present in the document text, with appropriate binary scoring (1.0 if found, 0.0 otherwise)
Expected value is semantically correct: metadata confirms 'American Gods' (3797.3 words/day) is the slowest Fantasy book, slower than 'Fire and Blood' (4797.59 words/day)
Postconfig appropriately activates Writer window and saves document with Ctrl+S, ensuring file content is written to disk before getter reads it
Complete coverage: evaluator verifies the final required outcome (correct book title recorded in DOCX)

Static warning about parameter type is a false positive: when expected.type='rule', framework calls get_rule() which returns config['rules'] directly, so metric correctly receives {'title': 'American Gods'} and accesses it via expected.get('title', '')
